title: OES-32 Dashboard: PyQt6 desktop view of a filtered synthetic 32-channel signal and its Welch PSD
description:
OES-32 Dashboard is a self-contained PyQt6 + PyQtGraph desktop application that shows a rolling filtered waveform (channel 0) and a channel-averaged Welch power spectral density (0-50 Hz) for a simulated 32-channel signal.

The GUI-free signal path (oes32_pipeline.py) applies a stateful 50 Hz IIR notch (Q = 30) and a 4th-order 0.5-45 Hz Butterworth bandpass at a nominal 250 Hz. The synthetic input is a 10 Hz test tone plus a 50 Hz mains-like tone in arbitrary units.

Scope: synthetic stimuli only. It is not hardware, field, medical or certified control software, makes no physical, biological or clinical claim, and is not the normative OES-32 residual (see oes32-residual).

Python 3.10+, PyQt6, PyQtGraph, NumPy and SciPy. pytest tests of the signal path and a headless start-up smoke test run in GitHub Actions. License: AGPL-3.0-only (commercial licence available).
